newsitem.title: UK: Yugoslav finance minister leaves for IMF talks.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslav finance minister leaves for IMF talks.

text.p: Yugoslav Finance Minister Tomica Raicevic left for Washington on Monday night for talks with senior International Monetary Fund (IMF) officials, a spokesman for the Yugoslav government told Reuters.
Last week the parliament of rump Yugoslavia, which comprises only Serbia and tiny Montenegro, approved what the government says are all the necessary conditions for joining the IMF.
Membership is a crucial step in Belgrade's efforts to bring in foreign capital to repair its economy, crippled by international sanctions imposed because of its role in the war in Bosnia.
"There is quite a strong sense of pragmatism coming through now (in the Yugoslav government). The signals back from the IMF have been quite positive," the spokesman said.
Raicevic is due to start talks with senior Fund officials on Wednesday.
Belgrade is also in the throes of negotiating a deal with commercial creditors to settle about $2 billion in debts inherited from the former Yugoslavia.
Bankers say a mountain of issues still have to be resolved, including how to share out the assets left behind after the old Yugoslavia's bloody collapse five years ago.
Even with membership of the IMF, Yugoslavia will still have to make some painful reforms before it is likely to get any financial help from the IMF.
